paragraphs: A dialog is a focused window layered over the page that blocks interaction until a task or decision is resolved.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: A dialog interrupts the page to focus the user on exactly one task or decision. It's the most disruptive surface available — it blocks everything else until it's resolved — so use it sparingly.

sections.heading: Types
paragraphs: Embedded form fields; the only type with an Error state.
A full-height panel (800px tall) in three widths.

sections.heading: Footer patterns
paragraphs: Information to be aware of; no decision
An action is needed to complete and close
The user must actively acknowledge something
Cancel + Previous + Next (or the completing action on the last step)

sections.heading: When to use
paragraphs: •   To get an immediate response needed to continue something the user just started.
•   To notify the user of urgent information tied to their current work.
•   To confirm a decision — especially a destructive or irreversible one.

sections.heading: When not to use
paragraphs: •   For information that isn't urgent — use an inline Alert instead.
•   For tasks users repeat often — let them complete it on the page.
•   When even the largest size isn't enough room — use a full page.

sections.heading: Anatomy
paragraphs: •   ① Title — a short, specific verb phrase naming the task.
•   ② Subtitle (optional) — short context below the title (Has subtitle).
•   ③ Close icon — always available for dismissal.
•   ④ Body — message text and/or embedded content such as form fields.
•   ⑤ Secondary action — e.g. Cancel, on the left.
•   ⑥ Primary action — the one action that completes the task, on the right.
Not shown: the overlay — the dimmed layer behind the dialog. It isn't built as a component yet.

sections.heading: Sizes
paragraphs: Choose the size by content: brief text fits Small; complex embedded content needs Medium or Large. If content keeps scrolling, move up a size; if the largest isn't enough, use a full page.

sections.heading: Alignment
paragraphs: Right-aligned, about half the footer width
Secondary left, primary right, each about half, flush to the edges
Each about a quarter, clustered right; only the rightmost may be primary
Cancel (ghost) alone on the left; Previous (secondary) and Next (primary) on the right

sections.heading: Placement
paragraphs: Center the dialog vertically for short, predictable content, or pin it at a fixed offset from the top for longer or variable content. Use a dimmed backdrop by default. Clicking the backdrop may close passive dialogs, but never transactional or destructive ones. Avoid opening a dialog from inside another dialog.
Secondary (Cancel) on the left, primary on the right — one clear emphasis.
Don't use two primary buttons — the user can't tell which action is safe.
For destructive actions, name the action in the title and use a danger-styled, specific button.
Don't use vague titles or buttons like OK for a destructive action.

sections.heading: Main elements
paragraphs: •   A short, specific verb phrase that matches whatever opened the dialog.
•   For a very short message, let the title carry it and skip the body.
•   Only when the purpose isn't obvious from the title.
•   Brief — only the fields and content needed to complete the task.
•   Short, specific verbs — Delete, Save, Add — not vague labels like Done.
•   OK is fine only for the acknowledgment pattern.

sections.heading: Overflow content
paragraphs: When the body needs to scroll, the header and footer stay fixed and only the body scrolls, with a fade at the bottom edge. Content never scrolls horizontally — move up a size instead.

sections.heading: States
paragraphs: •   Loading — the footer buttons are disabled while the action runs, preventing a double submit.
•   Error — Form only: an error banner at the top of the body, with the fields to correct.
See the Style tab for how each state looks.

sections.heading: Interactions
paragraphs: •   Opens only as the direct result of a user action — never unprompted.
•   Initial focus lands on the first form field, or on the primary button if there's no form.
•   Focus stays inside the dialog while it's open; on close it returns to the trigger.
•   Close with the close icon, Escape, or — for passive dialogs only — a click outside. Cancel reverts any staged changes.
•   Validate before closing on submit; keep the dialog open and mark fields in error.
•   Background page scroll is locked while the dialog is open.

sections.heading: Related
paragraphs: •   Alert — for inline, non-urgent feedback that shouldn't interrupt the page.
•   Button — used for the footer actions.

sections.heading: Color
paragraphs: Swatches are bound to the live tokens.
Footer buttons are Button instances; their colors belong to the Button component.

sections.heading: Variants & states
paragraphs: 30 variants: Type (5) × Size × State. Confirmation, Alert and Side-drawer have Open and Loading at Small, Medium and Large; Form adds Error; Full-screen has one Full size.

sections.heading: What the design system provides
paragraphs: •   A close icon on every type, alongside Escape.
•   Footer actions are real Buttons, with their focus and disabled states.
•   A Loading state that disables the footer buttons to prevent double submits.
•   A Form Error state with a text error banner, not color alone.

sections.heading: Development considerations
paragraphs: •   Use role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby pointing to the title.
•   Trap focus inside the dialog; return focus to the trigger on close.
•   Exclude background content from the accessibility tree while a decision is required — not just dim it.
•   The close icon is icon-only — give it an accessible name.
•   Set initial focus on the first field, or the primary button when there's no form.

sections.heading: Design recommendations
paragraphs: Automated contrast check — WCAG 2.x relative luminance (sRGB), text and icon against the dialog container, container against the page surface, for every theme combination. Minimums: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for the icon and container edge. Note: project-a / light is measured against the current surface/bg/default, which resolves to blue because of the gray/50 token.
Where the container edge is below 3:1, the overlay and drop shadow have to separate the dialog from the page.
